title: Reward Hacking in the Era of Large Models: Mechanisms, Emergent Misalignment, Challenges

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing length-quality correlations across training iterations and investigating how response length acts as a confounding variable that distorts actual reward scores in both standard reward models and process reward models (PRMs).

Using single-turn forced-choice benchmarks (e.g., the Beacon framework) to isolate the trade-off between factual accuracy and submissive agreement, and employing quantitative evaluation frameworks like SycEval to measure model sycophancy across diverse domains.
